properties.text: For all transactions tx submitted to the txpool: if tx.gasLimit > 16777216 (GAS_CAP), then the txpool MUST reject tx and tx MUST NOT be included in any candidate block.

reachability.notes: An attacker can submit transactions with arbitrary gasLimit values via P2P gossip or RPC. This is the first line of defense for EIP-7825.

properties.severity_justification: Bypassing the gas cap at the txpool layer allows oversized transactions to reach block builders, potentially enabling resource exhaustion attacks that could crash nodes or cause consensus failures if block validation is also bypassed.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating a transaction with gasLimit > 16777216 being admitted to the txpool.

properties.text: For all blocks B accepted as valid: for all transactions tx in B.transactions, tx.gasLimit <= 16777216 (GAS_CAP). A single violating transaction MUST invalidate the entire block.

reachability.notes: A malicious block builder can construct blocks with gas-cap-violating transactions and broadcast them via P2P. All validating nodes must independently reject such blocks.

properties.severity_justification: Failure to reject a block with a gas-cap-violating transaction at the consensus level would allow resource exhaustion attacks at scale, potentially crashing validators and fragmenting the network.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating a block with tx.gasLimit > 16777216 being accepted by a validator.

properties.text: Block validation MUST iterate over ALL transactions in the block before accepting it. There MUST NOT exist an early-exit optimization that could skip checking some transactions for the gas cap.

reachability.notes: An attacker could place a valid transaction first and a gas-cap-violating transaction later in the block, hoping an early-exit optimization skips validation of later transactions.

properties.severity_justification: An early-exit bug in block validation could allow a carefully ordered block to bypass gas cap enforcement for specific transaction positions.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating that a block with a violating transaction at a specific index bypasses validation due to early exit.

properties.text: The gas cap value GAS_CAP = 16777216 (2^24) MUST be identical at both the txpool validation layer (SG-001) and the block validation layer (SG-002). Divergence in the cap value between layers MUST NOT occur.

reachability.notes: This is a code-level consistency property. Divergence would be an implementation bug rather than an externally exploitable vulnerability, but could cause consensus splits.

properties.severity_justification: Divergent gas cap values between enforcement layers would cause blocks that pass one check to fail the other, leading to network partitions and consensus failures.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating a client implementation where the constant diverges between layers.

properties.text: The gas cap enforcement MUST be independent of the block gas limit. For all transactions tx: tx.gasLimit > 16777216 implies rejection, regardless of the current block gas limit value set by validators.

reachability.notes: An attacker could attempt to submit a transaction with gasLimit just above the cap when block gas limit is high, hoping the check compares against block gas limit instead of the protocol constant.

properties.severity_justification: If the gas cap check is accidentally tied to the block gas limit rather than the protocol constant, the cap could be bypassed when validators increase the block gas limit.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate that a transaction with gasLimit > 16777216 is accepted when block gas limit exceeds this value.

properties.text: The gas cap MUST apply uniformly to all transaction types: Legacy, EIP-2930 (AccessList), EIP-1559 (FeeMarket), EIP-4844 (Blob), and EIP-7702 (SetCode). No transaction type MUST be exempt from the cap.

reachability.notes: An attacker could submit a transaction using a specific type (e.g., blob transaction) with gasLimit > 16777216, hoping that type-specific validation bypasses the generic gas cap check.

properties.severity_justification: If any transaction type is exempt from the gas cap, it becomes a vector for resource exhaustion attacks using that specific type.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate that a specific transaction type can bypass the gas cap enforcement.

properties.text: The gas cap MUST be enforced at exactly two layers: (1) txpool admission and (2) block validation. Defense-in-depth requires that bypassing one layer does NOT compromise the system.

reachability.notes: In private transaction channels (e.g., Flashbots, MEV-Boost), transactions may bypass the txpool entirely. Block-level validation is the ultimate enforcement point.

properties.severity_justification: If both enforcement layers can be bypassed (e.g., via a private channel that skips txpool and a block validation bug), the gas cap is completely ineffective.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate a path where a transaction with gasLimit > 16777216 reaches execution without being caught by either layer.

properties.text: A transaction rejected at the txpool layer MUST NOT reach block validation. Once rejected, the transaction MUST NOT leak into the block building pipeline through any code path (race conditions, bypass paths, or buffer overflows).

reachability.notes: An attacker could exploit race conditions in concurrent txpool access or memory corruption to cause a rejected transaction to be processed despite failing the gas cap check.

properties.severity_justification: A TOCTOU (time-of-check-time-of-use) race condition in txpool rejection could allow gas-cap-violating transactions to enter the block building pipeline.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate a race condition or bypass that allows a rejected transaction to reach block building.

properties.text: The txpool gasLimit check MUST NOT have integer overflow, off-by-one, or type confusion vulnerabilities. The comparison tx.gasLimit > 16777216 MUST be semantically correct for all valid uint64 gasLimit values.

reachability.notes: An attacker submits a transaction with a specially crafted gasLimit value (e.g., near uint64 max, 0, or exactly 16777216) to trigger edge cases in the comparison logic.

properties.severity_justification: An integer overflow in the comparison could allow gasLimit values exceeding the cap to pass validation, completely undermining EIP-7825.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate an integer overflow or type confusion that causes the gas cap check to accept an oversized gasLimit.

properties.text: For all valid inputs to calculate_multiplication_complexity: multiplication_complexity >= 16. This minimum bound MUST hold regardless of base_length and modulus_length values.

reachability.notes: An attacker can invoke the ModExp precompile with arbitrary base_length and modulus_length values to attempt to produce a multiplication_complexity below 16.

properties.severity_justification: A multiplication_complexity below 16 would undercharge gas for ModExp operations, enabling resource exhaustion attacks (gas mispricing).
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate inputs where multiplication_complexity < 16 in any client implementation.

properties.text: For max(base_length, modulus_length) <= 32: multiplication_complexity MUST equal exactly 16 (fixed value, no formula computation needed).

reachability.notes: An attacker provides small base_length and modulus_length values (<= 32) and expects the gas cost to be at least multiplication_complexity = 16.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect handling of the small-input branch could lead to gas mispricing, but the impact is bounded because small inputs are computationally cheap.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate that for inputs with max_length <= 32, the multiplication_complexity is not 16 in any client.

properties.text: For max(base_length, modulus_length) > 32: multiplication_complexity MUST equal 2 * ceil(max_length/8)^2. The formula MUST use integer ceiling division and 2x multiplier (not the old EIP-2565 formula).

reachability.notes: An attacker can provide large base_length or modulus_length values to test the quadratic scaling formula. Incorrect implementation could lead to underpricing.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect quadratic scaling for large inputs was the primary vulnerability addressed by EIP-7883. Underpricing large-input ModExp enables DoS attacks.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate inputs where the computed multiplication_complexity differs from 2 * ceil(max_length/8)^2 in any client.

properties.text: For all valid inputs to calculate_iteration_count: iteration_count >= 1. The max(iteration_count, 1) clamp MUST be applied for large exponents to prevent zero-cost execution paths.

reachability.notes: An attacker could craft inputs with exponent == 0 or large exponent_length with zero top bytes, attempting to produce iteration_count == 0.

properties.severity_justification: An iteration_count of 0 would make the gas cost formula evaluate to 0 * complexity = 0, allowing free ModExp computation and enabling severe DoS attacks.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate inputs where iteration_count < 1 in any client implementation.

properties.text: For exponent_length <= 32 and exponent == 0: iteration_count MUST equal exactly 1 (not 0). The zero exponent edge case MUST be explicitly handled.

reachability.notes: An attacker provides exponent == 0 with exponent_length <= 32, expecting bit_length(0) - 1 = -1, which would cause underflow if not handled.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect handling of zero exponent could cause integer underflow (bit_length(0) - 1 = -1) leading to gas mispricing or crash.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate that exponent == 0 causes incorrect iteration_count or crash in any client.

properties.text: The large exponent multiplier in calculate_iteration_count MUST be 16 (doubled from EIP-2565's value of 8). The formula for exponent_length > 32 MUST be: 16 * (exponent_length - 32) + bit_length(top_32_bytes).

reachability.notes: An attacker with a large exponent would benefit from the old multiplier of 8, which underpriced large-exponent operations. Client implementations must use the new value of 16.

properties.severity_justification: Using the old multiplier of 8 instead of 16 would undercharge large-exponent ModExp operations by 50%, directly enabling the DoS attacks that EIP-7883 was designed to prevent.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate that any client uses multiplier 8 instead of 16 for large exponents post-Fusaka activation.

properties.text: The final gas cost for ModExp MUST be: max(500, floor(multiplication_complexity * iteration_count)). The minimum gas floor is 500 (raised from 200). There MUST be no division by 3.

reachability.notes: An attacker invokes ModExp with inputs designed to test the gas floor. If the old formula (with /3 divisor or 200 minimum) is used, the gas cost would be significantly lower.

properties.severity_justification: Using the old formula (with /3 divisor) would make ModExp roughly 3x cheaper than intended, directly enabling resource exhaustion attacks that EIP-7883 was designed to prevent.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate that any client post-Fusaka uses the old formula with /3 divisor or 200 minimum instead of the new formula.

properties.text: The gas cost formula for ModExp MUST NOT include the /3 divisor from EIP-2565. The formula MUST be max(500, floor(complexity * iterations)) NOT max(200, floor(complexity * iterations / 3)).

reachability.notes: The removal of /3 is one of the most impactful changes in EIP-7883. An implementation that retains the /3 would be severely underpricing ModExp.

properties.severity_justification: Retaining the /3 divisor would make all ModExp operations 3x cheaper than intended, creating a severe gas mispricing vulnerability exploitable for network-wide DoS.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate that any client retains the /3 divisor in the ModExp gas formula post-Fusaka.

properties.text: For identical ModExp inputs (base_length, modulus_length, exponent_length, exponent), all client implementations MUST compute the identical gas cost. Non-determinism in gas computation between clients MUST NOT exist.

reachability.notes: An attacker could craft ModExp inputs that trigger edge cases in integer arithmetic (ceiling division, floor, multiplication overflow) where different client implementations might diverge.

properties.severity_justification: Non-deterministic gas computation between clients would cause consensus splits: some nodes accept a block while others reject it due to different gas accounting.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate ModExp inputs where two different client implementations compute different gas costs.

properties.text: The gas cost calculation for ModExp MUST NOT have integer overflow vulnerabilities. The computation 2 * words^2 and complexity * iterations MUST use sufficiently large integer types (256-bit or arbitrary precision) to prevent wraparound to small values.

reachability.notes: An attacker provides very large base_length/modulus_length values (bounded by calldata/gas limit) attempting to cause 2 * words^2 to overflow, wrapping to a small gas cost.

properties.severity_justification: Integer overflow in gas cost computation could allow expensive ModExp operations to be executed for negligible gas, enabling severe DoS attacks.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate inputs where integer overflow causes the computed gas cost to be significantly lower than expected.

properties.text: EIP-7825 and EIP-7883 MUST be activated simultaneously at the Fusaka hard fork block. Inconsistent activation across nodes MUST NOT occur. Blocks straddling the activation boundary MUST apply the correct rules.

reachability.notes: Fork activation inconsistency is a configuration/deployment issue rather than a direct external attack vector. However, it could be exploited by a prepared attacker at the fork boundary.

properties.severity_justification: Inconsistent fork activation would cause a chain split where nodes running different rule sets diverge, fragmenting the network.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating a client that activates EIP-7825/7883 at the wrong block.

properties.text: A transaction with gasLimit == 16777216 (exactly at the cap) MUST be accepted by both the txpool and block validation. Only transactions with gasLimit > 16777216 (strictly greater) MUST be rejected.

reachability.notes: Off-by-one error in the comparison (>= instead of >) would reject valid transactions at exactly the cap boundary, causing unnecessary transaction failures.

properties.severity_justification: An off-by-one error would either reject valid transactions (at exactly 16777216) or accept invalid ones (at 16777217), both causing protocol violations.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate that a transaction with gasLimit == 16777216 is incorrectly rejected, or gasLimit == 16777217 is accepted.

properties.text: The txpool MUST NOT admit transactions with gasLimit > 16777216 regardless of the submission method: RPC, P2P gossip, or direct internal submission. All entry paths to the txpool MUST enforce the cap.

reachability.notes: An attacker could try different submission methods to find a path that bypasses the gas cap check.

properties.severity_justification: If any txpool entry path bypasses the gas cap check, the first layer of defense is undermined.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate a txpool entry path that does not enforce the gas cap.

properties.text: ModExp gas cost with the EIP-7883 formula MUST always be >= the EIP-2565 gas cost for the same inputs. The EIP-7883 changes (no /3, min 500, multiplier 16) MUST make all operations equal or more expensive than before.

reachability.notes: This is a monotonicity property. Any input where EIP-7883 gas cost < EIP-2565 gas cost indicates an implementation error.

properties.severity_justification: If any input produces a lower gas cost under EIP-7883 than EIP-2565, the security improvement is negated for those inputs, potentially re-enabling DoS vectors.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate inputs where EIP-7883 gas cost < EIP-2565 gas cost in any client.

properties.text: The ceil(max_length / 8) computation in calculate_multiplication_complexity MUST use integer ceiling division. For max_length = 33, words MUST equal 5 (not 4). Incorrect rounding would cause systematic undercharging.

reachability.notes: An attacker provides max_length values at the boundary of 8-byte words (e.g., 33, 41, 49) to test whether ceiling division is correctly implemented.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect rounding (floor instead of ceiling) would systematically undercharge gas for inputs not aligned to 8-byte boundaries.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate inputs where ceil(max_length/8) is computed incorrectly in any client.

properties.text: Smart contracts invoking ModExp MUST be charged gas according to the EIP-7883 formula post-Fusaka. Smart contracts MUST NOT bypass the gas cost increase by any mechanism (e.g., cached results, precomputed tables).

reachability.notes: An attacker invokes ModExp via a smart contract, attempting to exploit any gas cost bypass mechanism.

properties.severity_justification: Any mechanism to bypass the EIP-7883 gas cost increase would re-enable the DoS attacks that the EIP was designed to prevent.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate a method to invoke ModExp for less gas than the EIP-7883 formula specifies.

properties.text: The bit_length function used in calculate_iteration_count MUST return 0 for exponent == 0, and must return the position of the highest set bit + 1 for nonzero exponents. Incorrect bit_length would cause gas mispricing.

reachability.notes: An attacker crafts exponents with specific bit patterns (e.g., single high bit set, all bits set, alternating bits) to test bit_length correctness.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect bit_length computation would cause systematic gas mispricing for all non-trivial exponents.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate incorrect bit_length computation causing gas mispricing for specific exponent values.

properties.text: For exponent_length > 32: the top_32_bytes used in calculate_iteration_count MUST be extracted correctly from the exponent's most significant 32 bytes. Incorrect extraction (wrong endianness, wrong offset) would cause gas mispricing for large exponents.

reachability.notes: An attacker provides a large exponent where the top 32 bytes have a specific pattern that would produce different gas costs depending on extraction endianness.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect top-32-byte extraction for large exponents would systematically misprice the most expensive ModExp operations.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate incorrect top_32_bytes extraction causing gas mispricing for specific large exponents.

properties.text: The ModExp precompile MUST correctly compute base^exponent mod modulus for all valid inputs. The EIP-7883 gas cost increase MUST NOT alter the computational result; it only changes the gas charged.

reachability.notes: A regression in computational correctness alongside the gas change would break existing smart contracts.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect ModExp computation would break RSA verification, ZK proof systems, and other cryptographic operations relying on the precompile, potentially causing fund loss.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate that the ModExp result differs from the expected mathematical result for any input.

properties.text: In private transaction channels (Flashbots, MEV-Boost relays), transactions that bypass the txpool MUST still be caught by block-level gas cap validation. Block validation MUST serve as the ultimate enforcement point regardless of how transactions enter the block.

reachability.notes: An attacker submits gas-cap-violating transactions through private channels directly to a block builder, bypassing the txpool entirely.

properties.severity_justification: If block validation does not catch gas-cap-violating transactions that bypassed the txpool via private channels, the gas cap is completely ineffective for MEV/PBS transactions.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate a gas-cap-violating transaction reaching execution via a private channel without block validation catching it.

properties.text: In MEV-Boost/PBS architectures, the relay MUST validate gas cap compliance, or the proposer's own validation MUST catch gas-cap-violating transactions before signing. A proposer MUST NOT blindly sign a block containing gas-cap-violating transactions.

reachability.notes: A malicious block builder constructs a block with gas-cap-violating transactions and submits it through a relay, hoping the proposer blindly signs without validation.

properties.severity_justification: If a proposer signs a block with gas-cap-violating transactions, the block would be rejected by attesters, causing the proposer to lose their slot and MEV revenue.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate a path where a proposer signs a block with gas-cap-violating transactions due to insufficient validation.

properties.text: At maximum transactions at the gas cap (gasLimit = 16777216 each), a standard block (30M gas limit) MUST NOT be able to fit more than 1-2 transactions at the cap. The block gas limit MUST provide an implicit bound on the aggregate gas cap impact.

reachability.notes: An attacker packs a block with max-gasLimit transactions to maximize validation and execution overhead.

properties.severity_justification: The block gas limit naturally constrains the damage from gas-cap-sized transactions, but if the block gas limit is significantly increased, more cap-sized transactions could fit.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate that more transactions at the gas cap can fit in a block than expected due to block gas limit interactions.

properties.text: Smart contracts that previously relied on specific ModExp gas costs (pre-EIP-7883) MUST NOT have their security guarantees violated by the gas cost increase. The increase MUST only affect gas economics, not computational correctness.

reachability.notes: Contracts that hard-code gas amounts for ModExp calls may run out of gas post-EIP-7883. While this is expected behavior, it should not cause security-relevant failures.

properties.severity_justification: Contracts with hard-coded gas for ModExp calls will fail post-upgrade, but this is expected and documented. Security-relevant failures (e.g., in signature verification) would be more serious.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate a security-relevant contract failure caused by the gas cost increase beyond expected out-of-gas behavior.

properties.text: The EVM MUST enforce that a transaction cannot consume more gas than its declared gasLimit. The EIP-7825 cap applies to the declared gasLimit field, not to actual gas consumed. No re-entrancy, gas stipend, or other mechanism MUST allow consumption exceeding the declared gasLimit.

reachability.notes: An attacker could attempt to bypass the gas cap through re-entrancy or gas stipend mechanisms that cause actual gas consumption to exceed the declared gasLimit.

properties.severity_justification: If actual gas consumption can exceed the declared gasLimit, the gas cap is ineffective at bounding per-transaction resource usage.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate that actual gas consumption exceeds the declared gasLimit through any mechanism.

properties.text: The txpool MUST NOT be vulnerable to flooding attacks where high volumes of transactions at or near the gasLimit cap overwhelm storage, eviction logic, or network bandwidth. Standard txpool protections (size limits, fee-based eviction, per-sender nonce sequencing) MUST remain effective.

reachability.notes: An attacker floods the txpool with valid transactions (gasLimit <= 16777216) at high volume to overwhelm the txpool.

properties.severity_justification: Txpool flooding is a known DoS vector, but the gas cap does not make it worse. Standard mempool protections apply.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate a txpool flooding attack that bypasses standard protections due to gas cap interactions.

properties.text: Block validation MUST be deterministic and independently verifiable by all nodes. The gas cap check result for any given block MUST be the same across all compliant implementations. Non-deterministic block validation MUST NOT exist.

reachability.notes: Non-deterministic validation could cause some nodes to accept and others to reject the same block.

properties.severity_justification: Non-deterministic block validation would cause consensus splits, fragmenting the network.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate that two compliant implementations produce different validation results for the same block.

properties.text: The ModExp precompile MUST NOT exhibit timing side-channels that leak information about the exponent or other sensitive inputs to co-located observers through execution time variations.

reachability.notes: ModExp operates on public blockchain data. Input confidentiality is not a primary concern as all inputs are visible on-chain. However, timing oracles could be exploitable.

properties.severity_justification: All ModExp inputs are public on-chain, so timing side-channels do not leak additional secret information. However, timing oracles could theoretically be exploited in specific scenarios.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: ModExp inputs are public. Timing side-channels have limited security impact in this context.

properties.text: A transaction at the exact gas cap boundary (gasLimit == 16777216) submitting a ModExp call MUST have sufficient gas for the EIP-7883 gas cost. The interaction between the gas cap and ModExp gas pricing MUST NOT create scenarios where valid ModExp operations are impossible.

reachability.notes: The intersection of EIP-7825 (gas cap) and EIP-7883 (increased ModExp cost) could create edge cases where legitimate ModExp operations that fit within the gas cap under old pricing no longer fit.

properties.severity_justification: If the gas cap prevents legitimate large ModExp operations, it could break existing use cases (RSA verification, ZK proofs) that relied on larger gas limits.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate that a previously valid ModExp operation becomes impossible due to the combined effect of EIP-7825 and EIP-7883.

properties.text: At the Fusaka fork activation block, all transactions in the first post-fork block MUST be validated with the new gas cap rule (gasLimit <= 16777216). Pre-fork transactions in the txpool with gasLimit > 16777216 MUST be evicted or rejected when included in post-fork blocks.

reachability.notes: An attacker could submit pre-fork transactions with gasLimit > 16777216 and have them queued in the txpool, hoping they slip into the first post-fork block without re-validation.

properties.severity_justification: If pre-fork transactions are not re-validated after fork activation, gas-cap-violating transactions could be included in post-fork blocks, undermining EIP-7825.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate a pre-fork transaction with gasLimit > 16777216 being included in a post-fork block.

properties.text: The block validation gas cap check MUST operate on the raw transaction gasLimit field, not on a derived or computed value. The check MUST NOT be confused by EIP-1559 fee market semantics (effective_gas_price, max_fee_per_gas, max_priority_fee_per_gas) which are separate from gasLimit.

reachability.notes: An attacker could craft a transaction where the effective gas usage is below the cap but the declared gasLimit field exceeds it, testing whether the check operates on the correct field.

properties.severity_justification: Checking the wrong field (e.g., gas_used instead of gasLimit) would allow cap-violating transactions to pass validation.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Demonstrate that the gas cap check operates on a field other than tx.gasLimit.

properties.text: The ModExp gas cost formula MUST only use integer arithmetic operations: ceil(max_length / 8) for word count, integer multiplication for complexity, floor() for final cost, and max() for clamping. No floating-point arithmetic MUST be used in any step of the computation.

reachability.notes: Floating-point arithmetic in gas computation could introduce platform-dependent rounding differences, causing consensus splits.

properties.severity_justification: Floating-point arithmetic in consensus-critical code would cause non-determinism across platforms, leading to consensus splits.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating floating-point usage in gas computation in any client.
